title: CLO 2024 Academic Month: Digital Technology and Mutual Advancement in Teaching and Learning—On the Construction of the Fashion Digital Art Creative Practice Workshop
description: Review of CLO Academic Month 2024! Teacher Yang Xuemei from Huizhou University introduced the construction of the Digital Fashion Art Creative Practice Studio at Huizhou University—aimed at guiding students to learn independently, gradually forming a virtuous cycle where graduates start businesses that give back to teaching. Based on CLO digital garment technology and integrating industry, education, learning, and research experience, various innovative books and apps have been developed, which have proven effective in talent cultivation during the teaching process.

chunks.title: CLO 2024 Academic Month: Digital Technology and Mutual Advancement in Teaching and Learning—On the Construction of the Fashion Digital Art Creative Practice Workshop
chunks.content: ## Introduction to the Fashion Digital Art Creative Practice Workshop This section outlines the establishment, team composition, and key achievements of the Fashion Digital Art Creative Practice Workshop, emphasizing its integration of fashion, digital technology, and education. The Fashion Digital Art Creative Time Workshop, founded in 2009 at Huizhou Academy, Guangdong Fashion Academy, serves as a practical innovation platform integrating fashion, digitalization, teaching, research, and education. The teaching team is recognized at the provincial level, comprising 24 members including eight business professionals and three teaching consultants, aligned with the professional direction of clothing product processes. Key milestones include its designation as a key platform construction unit in Guangdong Province (2018), winning the Laomo and Craftsman Talent Innovation Workshop award (2020), and the Laomo and Craftsman Innovation Workshop award of Guangdong Province (2021). Due to a predominantly female teaching staff (76%), a female staff innovation workshop was also established. The workshop won second prize in the first Guangdong Province competition in 2023 and has hosted 38 social training events serving over 2,000 participants, despite pandemic-related restrictions. ## Development and Application of Digital Technology in Education This section details the workshop’s digital technology systems, virtual experiment platforms, and teaching reforms, highlighting their impact on fashion education and nationwide adoption. The workshop developed 10 virtual systems, including the Fashion, Fabric, Pattern, Creative, and Appliance Virtual Formatting Experiment. Recognized as a national first-class formatting course by the Guangdong Provincial Education Hall, this system serves as a competitive test platform for comprehensive training and ability assessment, used by over 50 colleges and thousands of students nationwide. It was among the top test systems nationwide in 2022. The program titled "Transformation of the Future of Education and Education" focuses on virtual formatting experiment teaching and quality sharing. Teaching reforms have been reported by Tencent News and Southern Urban News. Since 2021, the workshop has emphasized fashion design and engineering internal clothing professionalization, evolving from its 2008 announcement to become a leading national entity. ## Integration of Digital Technology into Clothing Education System This section explains the structural design of integrating digital technology into teaching concepts, textbooks, virtual environments, and experiential learning within the clothing education system. Clothing education encompasses teachers, students, courses, and environments, all integrated with digital technology. Teachers implement concepts supported by digital tools, materials, textbooks, experimental environments, and teaching resources unified under virtual technology. This creates an experiential teaching and learning method, enabling students to explore personal interests within a digital environment. Ten textbooks were developed with AR codes linking to app systems supported by network technology, transforming traditional paper textbooks into three-dimensional, dynamic learning resources. This approach connects the knowledge chain with the industrial chain to form a comprehensive knowledge system and an innovative three-dimensional teaching theory model aligned with industrialization. The teaching team covers materials, craftsmanship, design, sales, display, paper, and structure, applying virtual digital technology not only to textbooks but also to laboratories.

chunks.content: This creates an experiential teaching and learning method, enabling students to explore personal interests within a digital environment. Ten textbooks were developed with AR codes linking to app systems supported by network technology, transforming traditional paper textbooks into three-dimensional, dynamic learning resources. This approach connects the knowledge chain with the industrial chain to form a comprehensive knowledge system and an innovative three-dimensional teaching theory model aligned with industrialization. The teaching team covers materials, craftsmanship, design, sales, display, paper, and structure, applying virtual digital technology not only to textbooks but also to laboratories. Students access websites, operating systems, virtual experiments, an Artificial Intelligence Virtualization (AIV) system, and learning platforms, fostering collaborative group work. This model has won first prize in Huizhou City Teaching Achievement Awards for its innovative approach. ## Three-Dimensional Textbooks and Virtual Interaction This section illustrates the use of augmented reality (AR) and virtual systems in textbooks, enabling interactive and customizable learning experiences for students. Each textbook is paired with an app allowing students to scan images via smartphones to access additional knowledge. For example, clothing items can be viewed in three dimensions, adjusted in color, pattern, and style, enhancing practical application of learned content. Artificial intelligence programs analyze style structures virtually, providing structural analysis within the virtual systems. This integration enables students to query and explore content dynamically, blending virtual technology with traditional textbooks. ## Scientific Research and Virtual System Applications This section covers scientific research efforts, development of virtual systems across different professional directions, and the experimental application of digital technology in teaching. In 2021, the workshop’s research achievements were nationally recognized. Ten virtual systems were developed covering design, engineering, and performance directions, corresponding to the entire costume production process from design to final display. Virtual system demonstrations support students’ understanding of style structure, fabric, pattern, and color in historical internal clothing development. Experiments involve using materials from different eras for designing internal clothing products, bridging the gap between art and technology in traditional clothing education. This approach accelerates the transformation of theoretical knowledge into design practice, fostering innovation based on historical insight. The workshop also maintains a virtual exhibition system and an internal clothing virtual museum accessible via mobile phones, allowing students to review senior and graduate design works, thereby enriching educational resources. ## Student Engagement, Entrepreneurship, and Professional Development This section discusses student participation, entrepreneurial initiatives, and the iterative teaching model fostering practical skills and professional growth. Data from 2023 indicates 57.6% of high school graduates follow professional directions after graduation, with 40% pursuing other paths over five to ten years. Consequently, professional knowledge is increasingly delivered via virtual platforms, websites, and app-integrated textbooks, enabling students to explore personal interests and preferences effectively. Since 2011, an industrialized education team model encourages group cooperation, allowing students to choose between design, craftsmanship, and other fields, circulating through four professional directions over four years. This cross-disciplinary teaching fosters entrepreneurial learning, where students simulate company operations, enhancing professional and creative abilities.

chunks.content: Data from 2023 indicates 57.6% of high school graduates follow professional directions after graduation, with 40% pursuing other paths over five to ten years. Consequently, professional knowledge is increasingly delivered via virtual platforms, websites, and app-integrated textbooks, enabling students to explore personal interests and preferences effectively. Since 2011, an industrialized education team model encourages group cooperation, allowing students to choose between design, craftsmanship, and other fields, circulating through four professional directions over four years. This cross-disciplinary teaching fosters entrepreneurial learning, where students simulate company operations, enhancing professional and creative abilities. Students form entrepreneurial teams, applying digital textbook technologies and virtual system modeling in real projects. These student-led initiatives reduce direct teacher intervention, emphasizing peer-to-peer learning and practical business experience. Within two years, five students co-founded a technology company in Huizhou, supporting teaching and promoting the educational model. ## Outcomes and Impact of the Workshop Model This section summarizes key achievements, student outcomes, and the integrated ecosystem connecting teaching, research, and entrepreneurship. Over the past four years, the workshop trained 160 students in modeling technology; 80 have joined relevant enterprises, while five formed a cooperative enterprise within the school. These students contributed to 14 technical standards incorporated into textbooks and virtual systems, significantly influencing teaching quality. Student involvement in the platform reached 30 to 40 participants in 2022, facilitating autonomous peer teaching and entrepreneurial skill development. The interactive model integrates teaching, research, and entrepreneurship, producing excellent educational and professional outcomes. The student-founded company, established in 2020, collaborates with universities including Huizhou Academy, offering five courses that operate independently of direct teacher instruction, based on 3D modeling curricula. ## Educational Philosophy and Future Directions This section presents the workshop’s educational philosophy emphasizing individualized learning, student autonomy, and the balance between teaching, research, and enterprise collaboration. The workshop prioritizes returning education to the individual, allowing students to discover and develop personal interests and hobbies within a supportive environment. Rather than relying on corporate demands, teaching focuses on understanding and adapting to students’ preferences, preparing them for genuine industry engagement. The educational model integrates teaching, research, and student entrepreneurship, creating a closed-loop iterative learning system. Students gain practical enterprise experience during school and, if desired, start businesses with senior support. This approach aligns with the workshop’s 13-year practice, demonstrating effective collaboration among teaching teams, students, and enterprises, fostering sustainable professional growth and innovation in fashion digital art education.

For example, clothing items can be viewed in three dimensions, adjusted in color, pattern, and style, enhancing practical application of learned content. Artificial intelligence programs analyze style structures virtually, providing structural analysis within the virtual systems. This integration enables students to query and explore content dynamically, blending virtual technology with traditional textbooks. ## Scientific Research and Virtual System Applications This section covers scientific research efforts, development of virtual systems across different professional directions, and the experimental application of digital technology in teaching. In 2021, the workshop’s research achievements were nationally recognized. Ten virtual systems were developed covering design, engineering, and performance directions, corresponding to the entire costume production process from design to final display. Virtual system demonstrations support students’ understanding of style structure, fabric, pattern, and color in historical internal clothing development. Experiments involve using materials from different eras for designing internal clothing products, bridging the gap between art and technology in traditional clothing education. This approach accelerates the transformation of theoretical knowledge into design practice, fostering innovation based on historical insight. The workshop also maintains a virtual exhibition system and an internal clothing virtual museum accessible via mobile phones, allowing students to review senior and graduate design works, thereby enriching educational resources. ## Student Engagement, Entrepreneurship, and Professional Development This section discusses student participation, entrepreneurial initiatives, and the iterative teaching model fostering practical skills and professional growth. Data from 2023 indicates 57.6% of high school graduates follow professional directions after graduation, with 40% pursuing other paths over five to ten years. Consequently, professional knowledge is increasingly delivered via virtual platforms, websites, and app-integrated textbooks, enabling students to explore personal interests and preferences effectively. Since 2011, an industrialized education team model encourages group cooperation, allowing students to choose between design, craftsmanship, and other fields, circulating through four professional directions over four years. This cross-disciplinary teaching fosters entrepreneurial learning, where students simulate company operations, enhancing professional and creative abilities. Students form entrepreneurial teams, applying digital textbook technologies and virtual system modeling in real projects. These student-led initiatives reduce direct teacher intervention, emphasizing peer-to-peer learning and practical business experience. Within two years, five students co-founded a technology company in Huizhou, supporting teaching and promoting the educational model. ## Outcomes and Impact of the Workshop Model This section summarizes key achievements, student outcomes, and the integrated ecosystem connecting teaching, research, and entrepreneurship. Over the past four years, the workshop trained 160 students in modeling technology; 80 have joined relevant enterprises, while five formed a cooperative enterprise within the school. These students contributed to 14 technical standards incorporated into textbooks and virtual systems, significantly influencing teaching quality. Student involvement in the platform reached 30 to 40 participants in 2022, facilitating autonomous peer teaching and entrepreneurial skill development. The interactive model integrates teaching, research, and entrepreneurship, producing excellent educational and professional outcomes. The student-founded company, established in 2020, collaborates with universities including Huizhou Academy, offering five courses that operate independently of direct teacher instruction, based on 3D modeling curricula. ## Educational Philosophy and Future Directions This section presents the workshop’s educational philosophy emphasizing individualized learning, student autonomy, and the balance between teaching, research, and enterprise collaboration. The workshop prioritizes returning education to the individual, allowing students to discover and develop personal interests and hobbies within a supportive environment. Rather than relying on corporate demands, teaching focuses on understanding and adapting to students’ preferences, preparing them for genuine industry engagement. The educational model integrates teaching, research, and student entrepreneurship, creating a closed-loop iterative learning system. Students gain practical enterprise experience during school and, if desired, start businesses with senior support. This approach aligns with the workshop’s 13-year practice, demonstrating effective collaboration among teaching teams, students, and enterprises, fostering sustainable professional growth and innovation in fashion digital art education.
